papers.title: Supernova Bounds on Neutrino Dipole Moments from a Modern Perspective
papers.abstract: Neutrinos may have nonstandard magnetic dipole moments $\mu_\nu$. In the dense cores of supernovae (SNe), these would convert part of the neutrinos into sterile, right-handed states through the electromagnetic fluctuations of the charged plasma. The streaming sterile neutrinos with 100-MeV energies can convert back to standard neutrinos in the Galactic magnetic field, leading to a high-energy neutrino flux unobserved from the historical SN 1987A. We reassess the production rates, including scattering on both protons and electrons, and, building upon advances in SN simulations and in the description of the Milky Way magnetic field, we revisit the bounds on magnetic dipole moments. We find for Dirac electron neutrinos $\mu_{\nu_e} \lesssim 4.8 \times 10^{-13} \mu_B$, superseding all existing terrestrial and astrophysical constraints.
papers.reason: Directly addresses supernova neutrino bounds on magnetic dipole moments, a core interest for this reader.

summary.tldr: We derive a new, stringent constraint on the electron neutrino magnetic dipole moment, $\mu_{\nu_e} \lesssim 4.8 \times 10^{-13} \mu_B$, using the non-observation of high-energy neutrinos from SN 1987A.
summary.novel_idea: This work updates the 1980s-era event-counting bounds on neutrino magnetic dipole moments by incorporating modern Garching 1D supernova simulations, updated Galactic magnetic field models, and improved production rates from scattering on both protons and electrons.
summary.method: The authors calculate the emissivity of right-handed neutrinos produced via helicity-flip scattering in the supernova core, propagate these sterile states through the Galactic magnetic field where they reconvert to active neutrinos, and compute the expected event rate in the IMB detector.
key_results: Constraint on electron neutrino magnetic moment: $\mu_{\nu_e} \lesssim 4.8 \times 10^{-13} \mu_B$ at 90% C.L.
The bound is a factor of 7 stronger than the traditional cooling bound.
Future sensitivity for a Galactic supernova at 10 kpc is estimated at $\sim 10^{-14} \mu_B$ for Hyper-Kamiokande.
summary.why_it_matters: This paper provides the most robust astrophysical constraint on $\mu_{\nu}$, which is highly relevant for BSM models involving dipole portals and neutrino electromagnetic properties, and it serves as a benchmark for future DUNE/Hyper-K supernova pointing and detection programs.
summary.caveats: The bounds depend on the assumed supernova model (cold vs. hot) and the uncertainty in the Galactic magnetic field integral.

papers.title: On the Structure of the Nuclear-Clock Isotope $^{229}$Th Beyond Quadratic Order
papers.abstract: Precision measurements of the exceptionally low-energy nuclear transition of $^{229}$Th, offer an extraordinary sensitivity to a variety of new light fields. However, interpreting such measurements requires nuclear-structure information beyond what is currently constrained by spectroscopy. We develop a systematic description of the electric multipole interactions governing the hyperfine structure of ${}^{229}$Th, including the hexadecapole contribution, and perform a symmetry-based analysis of the resulting hyperfine splittings in crystalline environments. Hyperfine spectroscopy generally constrains combinations of nuclear moments and crystal-field gradients, leading to degeneracies when higher multipole interactions are allowed. We then combine experimental nuclear observables, particle-rotor relations, and a deformed-Fermi charge-density model to investigate the electromagnetic contribution to the nuclear clock's sensitivity to variations in the fine-structure constant. We find that higher-order nuclear deformation and state-dependent differences in the radial charge distribution of the clock states can substantially alter the predicted sensitivity, introducing large uncertainties that are not constrained by existing measurements. Our results highlight the importance of combining nuclear and solid-state theory with complementary measurements, including spectroscopy of higher-spin states, to constrain the nuclear structure and improve predictions of the clock's sensitivity to new physics. Our symmetry-based analysis also provides a framework for using hyperfine spectroscopy to investigate local defect symmetries in crystalline hosts.
papers.reason: Directly addresses nuclear structure and precision probes of new physics, which are core interests. [favorite author: Gilad Perez]

summary.tldr: We develop a systematic multipole formalism for the $^{229}$Th nuclear clock, showing that hexadecapole interactions and nuclear structure uncertainties significantly impact the clock's sensitivity to new physics.
summary.novel_idea: The paper introduces a systematic electric multipole expansion for the $^{229}$Th clock states, including the hexadecapole contribution, and uses a deformed-Fermi charge-density model to relate spectroscopic observables to intrinsic nuclear structure.
summary.method: The authors employ a symmetry-based analysis of hyperfine splittings in crystalline environments and combine experimental nuclear observables with the particle-rotor model to constrain the nuclear charge distribution and estimate the sensitivity factor $\mathcal{K}$.
key_results: Hexadecapole interactions introduce degeneracies in extracting quadrupole moments from hyperfine spectroscopy.
Higher-order nuclear deformation and radial charge distribution differences significantly alter the predicted sensitivity to new physics.
Existing measurements are insufficient to fully constrain the intrinsic nuclear structure required for precision sensitivity predictions.
summary.why_it_matters: This is essential for the reader's interest in precision atomic/nuclear probes of new physics and the nuclear clock, as it quantifies the theoretical uncertainty in using $^{229}$Th to search for ultralight dark matter or variation of fundamental constants.
summary.caveats: The model relies on phenomenological assumptions for the charge distribution; further experimental data on higher-spin states is needed to break degeneracies.

papers.title: A Predictive Nuclear Effective Field Theory from Wilsonian Renormalization Group Principles I: Medium-mass nuclei and nuclear matter
papers.abstract: The predictive power of nuclear effective field theory (EFT) from few- to many-body systems is substantially restricted by regulator dependence. Wilsonian momentum-shell renormalization group (RG) offers a natural framework for cutoff-independent predictions, but its many-body implementation requires regulating single-particle momentum modes, which breaks Galilean invariance. RG scaling analysis shows that this symmetry breaking is encoded in irrelevant operators whose effects can be included explicitly or absorbed into higher-body interactions. Guided by Wilsonian RG, we construct a regularization scheme for chiral EFT contact interactions and predict binding energies of nuclei up to $^{40}$Ca using interactions calibrated only to $A\leq3$ systems. The predicted energies vary at the percent level and agree with experiment for $300\leq\Lambda\leq450$~MeV. The same scheme reduces the overbinding of symmetric nuclear matter obtained with conventional relative-momentum regulators. Our results suggest that some model dependence observed in nonrelativistic many-body calculations originates from treating EFT vertices as static, Galilean-invariant potentials rather than as field operators regulated consistently across particle-number sectors.
papers.reason: Directly addresses nuclear EFT and many-body systems, which are core interests.

summary.tldr: We demonstrate that using a universal single-particle absolute-momentum regulator in nuclear EFT leads to cutoff-independent binding energies for medium-mass nuclei and improves nuclear matter saturation.
summary.novel_idea: The authors propose replacing conventional Galilean-invariant relative-momentum regulators with a Wilsonian-inspired absolute-momentum regulator, which enables consistent RG flow across particle-number sectors.
summary.method: The study uses Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory (NLEFT) and Brueckner-Hartree-Fock (BHF) methods to compute binding energies and nuclear matter equations of state, calibrating interactions only to $A \leq 3$ systems.
key_results: Binding energies for nuclei up to $^{40}$Ca are stable within a few MeV for $300 \leq \Lambda \leq 450$ MeV.
The scheme reduces the overbinding of symmetric nuclear matter typically found with relative-momentum regulators.
Predictions for $^{40}$Ca binding energy: $-343.9(27)(25)$ MeV, in good agreement with experiment.
summary.why_it_matters: This directly addresses the reader's interest in neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling and event generators by providing a more robust, regulator-independent framework for ab initio nuclear structure calculations.
summary.caveats: The regulator breaks Galilean invariance explicitly, requiring the inclusion of symmetry-restoring operators or recalibration of 3NF counterterms.

papers.title: A Predictive Nuclear Effective Field Theory from Wilsonian Renormalization Group Principles II: Hidden unitary transformations
papers.abstract: A fundamental challenge in nuclear effective field theories (EFTs) is to demonstrate the equivalence of interactions built at different momentum cutoffs and calibrated to the same set of low-momentum observables. Focusing on contact terms, we explicitly construct the unitary transformation that connects these EFT Hamiltonians. By replacing the conventional \emph{relative}-momentum cutoff with a universal single-particle \emph{absolute}-momentum cutoff, we show that this transformation can be systematically implemented using the similarity renormalization group (SRG) technique. The key insight is that such a regularization scheme enables a manifest decoupling of the many-body Fock space, avoiding transitions of particles in intermediate states into high-momentum subspaces associated with conventional \emph{relative}-momentum regulators. The derivation closely parallels the momentum-shell integration formalism of the Wilsonian RG flow. Reformulating the path integral in terms of unitary transformations allows a more intuitive, energy-independent analysis of nonrelativistic many-body systems within the EFT framework. In particular, this framework ensures that effective interactions calibrated in few-body sectors remain unitarily equivalent when applied to many-body systems, a central requirement not yet fulfilled in nuclear many-body calculations. We also show that the breaking of Galilean invariance due to the \emph{absolute}-momentum regularization induces irrelevant operators controlled by the RG scaling behavior, without introducing further complications. We numerically demonstrate our theoretical analysis using a one-dimensional toy model of bosons. These results provide a useful tool for analyzing the RG evolution of nonrelativistic many-body systems.
papers.reason: Directly addresses nuclear EFT and unitary transformations, which are core interests.

summary.tldr: We derive the unitary transformations connecting nuclear EFT Hamiltonians at different cutoffs, showing that absolute-momentum regularization ensures consistent decoupling of many-body Fock space.
summary.novel_idea: The paper provides a constructive proof of RG invariance by explicitly constructing the unitary transformation (via SRG) that maps EFT Hamiltonians between different scales, keeping them energy-independent.
summary.method: The authors use a second-quantized Fock space decomposition and SRG flow equations to decouple low- and high-momentum sectors, verified numerically with a 1D bosonic toy model.
key_results: Demonstration that few-body calibrated interactions remain unitarily equivalent in many-body systems.
Formal derivation showing that Galilean-invariance-breaking terms are irrelevant operators in the RG sense.
Numerical confirmation that the framework yields cutoff-independent results in an exactly solvable model.
summary.why_it_matters: This provides the theoretical foundation for the regularization scheme in the companion paper (2611.22960), essential for the reader's interest in ab initio electroweak responses and nuclear structure.
summary.caveats: The framework is formal and requires careful implementation of symmetry-restoring counterterms for realistic 3D nuclear systems.

papers.title: Precision Muon Physics
papers.abstract: The muon has become a versatile tool for fundamental physics. Measurements of muon decay determine the Fermi constant and establish the chiral structure of weak interactions. Measurements with stored muons and bound muons enable precision determinations of the muon charge, mass, and magnetic moment. These studies also provide far-reaching tests of bound-state QED and the Standard Model, as well as unique sensitivity to physics beyond our current understanding of the particles, forces, and laws of nature. We survey the landscape of precision muon physics, emphasizing both the physics reach and the experimental breadth. We highlight the range of techniques, from charged-particle timing, tracking, and polarimetry to storage-ring experiments, microwave resonance methods, and Doppler-free laser spectroscopy. We also describe the interplay between experimental work and theoretical developments in quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and effective field theory.
papers.reason: This is squarely in the reader's core interest, covering precision muon measurements, electroweak interactions, and BSM sensitivity.

summary.tldr: This review surveys the landscape of precision muon physics, detailing how muon decay, muonium spectroscopy, and storage-ring measurements provide stringent tests of the Standard Model and sensitivity to BSM physics.
summary.novel_idea: The paper synthesizes the interplay between experimental techniques (timing, tracking, laser spectroscopy) and theoretical developments (QED, QCD, EFT) across the entire muon physics program.
summary.method: A comprehensive review of experimental methods and theoretical frameworks, including the history of muon experiments, facilities, and the status of $G_F$, $a_{\mu}$, and muonium spectroscopy.
key_results: Fermi constant $G_F$ determined to 0.5 ppm precision.
Muon anomalous magnetic moment $a_{\mu}$ measured to 124 ppb precision.
Muonium spectroscopy provides ppb-level tests of bound-state QED and mass ratios.
summary.why_it_matters: Highly relevant for the reader's interest in precision electroweak physics, BSM searches (dipole portals, dark photons), and the theoretical tools (EFT, QED) used to interpret these results.
summary.caveats: This is a broad survey rather than a research paper; it covers established results rather than new theoretical developments.

papers.title: Fundamental physics with quantum sensors in space
papers.abstract: Quantum sensors such as atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic magnetometers can be used as sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. Space offers microgravity, long baselines, low environmental noise, access to varying gravitational potentials, and unique opportunities involving the Sun, Moon, planets, and asteroids. These proceedings of the Aspen Center for Physics workshop on "Fundamental physics in space with quantum sensors," held February 22-27, 2026, summarize the scientific case, current capabilities, and space mission concepts for investigating dark matter, testing general relativity, and detecting gravitational waves in frequency bands inaccessible from the ground.
papers.reason: This is highly relevant as it discusses using quantum sensors (atomic clocks, interferometers) to probe BSM physics, which is a key interest. [favorite author: Yu-Dai Tsai]

summary.tldr: This workshop summary outlines the scientific case and mission concepts for using space-based quantum sensors—atomic clocks and atom interferometers—to probe dark matter, gravitational waves, and fundamental physics.
summary.novel_idea: The paper advocates for a unified space-based quantum sensing program, leveraging microgravity and long baselines to access gravitational-wave frequency bands (microhertz and decihertz) inaccessible from the ground. It highlights the potential for these sensors to detect ultralight dark matter via oscillations in fundamental constants and to test the equivalence principle with unprecedented precision.
summary.method: The authors synthesize discussions from an Aspen Center for Physics workshop, detailing the performance requirements for optical atomic clocks and atom interferometers. They evaluate mission concepts like CHRONOS and pathfinders like the Cold Atom Lab, while addressing the necessary technological developments in optical links and photonic integration.
key_results: Optical atomic clocks can reach fractional-frequency uncertainties below 10^-18, enabling tests of gravitational redshift at centimeter scales.
Space-based atom interferometers offer sensitivity gains of order 10^4 in phase response due to extended interrogation times in free fall.
Proposed missions target dark matter masses from 10^-23 to 10^-12 eV and gravitational-wave bands in the microhertz and decihertz ranges.
summary.why_it_matters: This is highly relevant to your interest in precision atomic probes of new physics and ultralight dark matter. The discussion on optical clock networks and atom interferometry provides a strategic roadmap for the next generation of experiments that could constrain BSM physics.
summary.caveats: The proposed missions require significant technological maturation, particularly in long-distance optical time-frequency transfer and the miniaturization of laser systems for flight.

papers.title: Flavor Entanglement as a CPT Violation Witness in Neutrino Oscillations
papers.reason: Directly links neutrino oscillations, CPT violation, and quantum entanglement, which are core interests.

summary.tldr: The authors propose using the single-particle flavor concurrence as a CPT-violation witness in neutrino oscillations, demonstrating that the entanglement asymmetry provides a clean, background-free signal of SME-type CPT violation.
summary.novel_idea: The paper introduces the concurrence as a more mathematically tractable entanglement measure than von Neumann entropy for CPT studies. It derives exact analytical relations linking entanglement asymmetry to probability asymmetry, baseline reflection sums, and the long-baseline decoherence floor, while identifying a 24-hour sidereal modulation as a definitive temporal signature to distinguish CPT effects from matter-induced backgrounds.
summary.method: The study utilizes a two-flavor oscillation framework with an effective Hamiltonian modified by CPT-odd SME coefficients. It employs first-order perturbation theory to derive analytical relations and validates these against numerical simulations using a DUNE-like baseline (1300 km) and realistic Earth density profiles (PREM).
key_results: Projects a 1-sigma sensitivity to SME CPT-odd parameters at the 10^-14 eV scale for DUNE-like experiments.
Identifies a 24-hour sidereal modulation of the entanglement asymmetry as a 'smoking gun' to disentangle CPT violation from Wolfenstein matter effects.
Demonstrates that the reflection-sum mismatch scales to ~10^13 meters at PeV energies, suggesting high potential for future neutrino telescopes.
Analytical relations for the entanglement asymmetry are validated with relative errors < 1% at 2.0 GeV.
summary.why_it_matters: This work is highly relevant to your interest in neutrino event generators and oscillation systematics, as it provides a new, robust observable for BSM physics that is theoretically distinct from standard probability-based analyses. It also touches on your interest in BSM portals and precision tests, offering a novel way to leverage long-baseline data for fundamental symmetry tests.
summary.caveats: The current framework is limited to a two-flavor approximation; extension to three-flavor oscillations with CP violation is required for realistic experimental application. The analysis assumes CPT-even decoherence, and any CPT-odd component in the dephasing parameter would introduce additional backgrounds.

papers.title: An exact separability criterion for the $J/\psi\Lambda$ spin state in $\Lambda_b^0\to J/\psi\,\Lambda$ decays at the LHC
papers.abstract: We derive an exact separability criterion for the spin state of the $J/\psi\Lambda$ pair produced in $\Lambda_b^0\to J/\psi(\to\mu^+\mu^-)\,\Lambda(\to p\pi^-)$ decays, taking into account the $\Lambda_b^0$ polarization at the LHC. Within the four-amplitude family $\{a_\pm,b_\pm\}$, the system is separable if and only if $(1+P_b\cos\theta)a_+b_+=(1-P_b\cos\theta)a_-b_-=P_b\sin\theta b_+b_-=0$, where $\theta$ is the $\Lambda$ production angle defined in the LHC environment. We propose a profiled likelihood ratio test to probe entanglement in the full five-dimensional angular analysis. Idealized pseudoexperiments compare this test with a negativity test and a test based on the angular moments $M_7$ and $M_9$ for rejecting the $a_+=b_-=0$ hypothesis. At both $3\sigma$ and $5\sigma$ significance, the proposed test achieves a $90\%$ rejection power with about half as many signal events as the other two methods. These results support the prospects for entanglement evidence with samples on the existing scale and for observation with larger samples.
papers.reason: Directly addresses quantum entanglement and spin correlations in scattering final states, a core interest.

summary.tldr: The authors derive an exact separability criterion for the $J/\psi\Lambda$ spin state in $\Lambda_b^0$ decays, proposing a profiled likelihood ratio test to probe entanglement at the LHC.
summary.novel_idea: The paper provides a necessary and sufficient condition for entanglement in the $2\otimes 3$ spin Hilbert space of the $J/\psi\Lambda$ system, accounting for $\Lambda_b^0$ polarization. It introduces a profiled likelihood ratio test that outperforms existing negativity and angular-moment tests in rejection power.
summary.method: The authors construct the spin-density matrix and apply the Peres-Horodecki (PPT) criterion. They map the entanglement condition to measured angular moments and compare the sensitivity of different statistical tests using idealized pseudoexperiments.
key_results: The separability criterion is defined by the vanishing of three transverse correlations: $C_{1,+1;-1}=C_{2,+1;-1}=C_{2,2;-1}=0$.
The proposed profiled likelihood test achieves 90% rejection power with approximately 50% fewer signal events than moment-based tests.
Reconstruction from existing LHCb data yields a median negativity of $\mathcal{N} \simeq 0.06$.
summary.why_it_matters: This is highly relevant to your interest in quantum entanglement and spin correlations in scattering final states, specifically within the context of LHCb physics.
summary.caveats: The study addresses entanglement rather than Bell nonlocality; a robust test of the latter requires further treatment of measurement settings and experimental uncertainties.

papers.title: Scalar inelastic scattering of pseudo-Majorana dark matter through a radion portal
papers.abstract: We investigate a radion portal for pseudo-Majorana dark matter as an interpretation of the high-recoil event LZ230616. In contrast to the familiar pseudo-Dirac regime, the pseudo-Majorana structure allows a dominant scalar transition while suppressing elastic scattering. Endothermic kinematics remove low-energy recoils, while the nuclear response shapes the surviving high-recoil spectrum. Combining the accepted LZ event count with the Born-level thermal relic abundance yields a reference solution with $m_\chi=1$ TeV, $\delta=340$ keV, and $m_r=30$ GeV. This solution lies within the published LZ spin-independent $\mathcal{O}_1^s$ interval and remains compatible with existing OPAL and CMS constraints, while a simplified HL-LHC diphoton projection could probe it. Solar neutrino searches offer a complementary test. The benchmark's energetic-daughter proxy rates are comparable in magnitude to the rate scales reconstructed from IceCube's direct $b\bar{b}$ and $\tau^+\tau^-$ templates. An illustrative IceCube-Gen2 rescaling suggests future sensitivity, while a model-specific assessment requires the radion-cascade neutrino spectra and detector response.
papers.reason: Directly addresses inelastic scattering and nuclear responses, which are core interests.

summary.tldr: The authors propose a radion portal for pseudo-Majorana dark matter to explain the LZ230616 event, utilizing endothermic scattering to filter low-energy recoils.
summary.novel_idea: Unlike pseudo-Dirac models, the pseudo-Majorana structure allows for an unsuppressed scalar transition while suppressing elastic scattering. This naturally produces a high-recoil signal without the expected population of low-energy events.
summary.method: The authors formulate a 4D effective theory with a radion portal to nearly degenerate Majorana states. They perform a joint analysis of the LZ event count and Born-level thermal relic abundance to constrain the parameter space $(m_{\chi}, \delta, m_r, \Lambda_r)$.
key_results: Reference solution found at $m_{\chi}=1$ TeV, $\delta=340$ keV, and $m_r=30$ GeV.
The model is compatible with LZ spin-independent $\mathcal{O}_1^s$ intervals and current collider constraints.
Predicts energetic-daughter proxy rates comparable to IceCube direct $b\bar{b}$ and $\tau^+\tau^-$ templates.
summary.why_it_matters: This paper aligns with your interests in BSM physics at neutrino experiments and dark matter phenomenology. The radion portal and the use of inelastic kinematics are sophisticated tools for interpreting anomalous direct-detection events.
summary.caveats: The model requires specific radion-cascade neutrino spectra for a definitive assessment against IceCube data; the current analysis relies on illustrative rescalings.

papers.title: Plugging the Pion Chimney
papers.abstract: Heavy QCD axions and other gluon-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses from MeV to GeV are well motivated and have been searched for extensively. However, a window around the neutral pion mass, the so-called pion chimney, has escaped every search. There the ALP mixes strongly with the $\pi^0$ and therefore shares its experimental signatures. We show that the chimney can be closed with existing LHC data. The key point is that mixing changes the lifetimes of the two mass eigenstates but does not make them equal, and at LHC energies the states are boosted enough for the lifetime to decide whether they escape the detector or decay inside it. The ATLAS monojet search constrains the first case and the ATLAS inclusive photon measurement the second, and together they exclude the chimney up to the cutoff of the ALP effective theory. Above the cutoff, LHC searches for the colored states of the simplest ultraviolet completions exclude the rest. We also show that the bound from the $K^+$ width does not reach the chimney, because an ALP passes the same selection as a $\pi^0$, and we derive an independent, purely kinematic constraint from the measured $\pi^\pm$-$\pi^0$ mass splitting.
papers.reason: Relevant to BSM searches at neutrino experiments and the reader's interest in pion-related physics.

summary.tldr: The authors demonstrate that the 'pion chimney'—a window around the neutral pion mass where gluon-coupled ALPs have escaped detection—can be closed using existing LHC data.
summary.novel_idea: The authors show that strong mixing between an ALP and $\pi^0$ does not equalize their lifetimes. At LHC energies, the boost makes the lifetime difference decisive: one mass eigenstate escapes the detector (monojet signature), while the other decays inside (inclusive photon signature).
summary.method: The authors diagonalize the ALP-$\pi^0$ mass matrix exactly to define mass eigenstates. They recast ATLAS monojet and inclusive photon measurements to constrain these eigenstates and derive an independent kinematic constraint from the measured $\pi^{\pm}$-$\pi^0$ mass splitting.
key_results: Excludes the pion chimney up to the effective theory cutoff ($c_{GG}/f \simeq 0.15$ GeV^-1).
Shows that the $K^+$ width bound does not reach the chimney because ALPs pass the same experimental selection as $\pi^0$.
Provides a purely kinematic constraint from the $\pi^{\pm}$-$\pi^0$ mass splitting that checks the narrowest part of the chimney.
summary.why_it_matters: This is a strong example of using precision meson physics and LHC data to close a BSM 'blind spot'. It is highly relevant to your interest in effective field theories and BSM physics at colliders.
summary.caveats: The constraints above the EFT cutoff rely on the assumption of minimal KSVZ-type UV completions.

papers.title: Probing scalar-mediated Lorentz violation with hydrogen masers and spin-precession of molecules
papers.abstract: We propose using hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession experiments, traditionally employed in precision frequency measurements and searches for the electron electric dipole moment, as complementary probes of light scalar-mediated, spin-dependent fifth forces. We investigate their sensitivity to Lorentz-violating interactions mediated by scalars with masses ranging from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4}~\mu\mathrm{eV})$ to $\mathcal{O}(10~\mathrm{keV})$. While hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession measurements probe different combinations of Lorentz-violating couplings, we find that the strongest projected sensitivities can be achieved using spin-precession of ultracold molecules, benefiting from their extended coherence times. These experimental approaches provide access to previously unexplored regions of parameter space, probing interaction ranges extending from centimeter to sub-angstrom scales. Our proposals highlight the potential of precision atomic and molecular experiments to search for new spin-dependent scalar-mediated interactions and violations of fundamental spacetime symmetries.
papers.reason: Precision atomic/molecular probes of new physics are a high-interest area for this reader.

papers.title: Millicharged Fermions as Dark Matter: Theoretical Modeling and Experimental Detection
papers.abstract: Fermions with a small effective charge, $\qeff\ll1$, arise from kinetic mixing between an unbroken (or nearly unbroken) dark $U(1)'$ and electromagnetism, or from a genuinely fractional charge. Millicharged particles (mCPs) inherit the Pauli-exclusion constraints on fermionic dark matter (DM) in galaxies, while adding a long-range plasma phenomenology absent for neutral candidates. This review connects three strands: (i) the symmetry structure, cosmology and astrophysical bounds of millicharged fermions, comparing kinetic-mixing and fractional-charge realizations; (ii) the role of mCPs in galactic halo formation and dynamics, and when they fit the Ruffini--Arg\"uelles--Rueda (RAR) self-gravitating core--halo model; and (iii) experimental techniques for detecting mCPs trapped on Earth, arriving from the galactic halo, or emitted by the Sun. We show that a collisionless halo of keV--MeV millicharged fermions requires $\alpha'\lesssim7\times10^{-13}$--$2\times10^{-10}$, depending on mass and velocity, orders of magnitude below the coupling needed for thermal freeze-out via $\chi\bar\chi\to A'A'$ in the Milky Way and dwarf galaxies. A RAR halo made of the mCP itself thus needs non-thermal production, a charge-symmetric plasma and very small dark coupling, whereas a sub-dominant mCP component can be added without changing the halo. We close with open theoretical and experimental challenges and a summary of the allowed mCP parameter space.
papers.reason: Relevant to BSM physics and dark matter, which are high-interest topics for this reader.

papers.title: A Universal Axion in a Twin-QCD Sector
papers.abstract: Dark matter may consist of multiple components with distinct particle-physics origins. We investigate a scenario in which a universal axion couples to both visible and twin QCD, with twin baryons providing a possible dominant dark-matter component. The presence of a second strongly interacting sector can substantially enhance the axion mass while preserving its role in resolving the strong-CP problem, provided the physical vacuum angles are appropriately aligned. For a representative uniformly rescaled twin spectrum with a confinement scale five times that of ordinary QCD, the axion mass is enhanced by approximately a factor of 25. Using lattice-informed QCD results and a two-temperature description of the early universe, we investigate the cosmological evolution and relative abundances of the dark-sector components. In a representative conditional numerical benchmark, axions account for a small percentage of the observed dark matter, while twin baryons could constitute the remainder for a suitable primordial baryon asymmetry. We also examine the implications for additional relativistic species, strong-CP alignment, and the interactions of stable twin matter. Our results provide a quantitative framework for exploring mixed axion--twin-baryon dark matter and identify the particle-physics and cosmological conditions necessary for a viable realization, including constraints from the thermal history and formation of cosmic structure.
papers.reason: Axion physics and dark matter are high-interest areas for this reader.

papers.title: Imprints of Non-local Top-Higgs Interaction on Loop Induced Higgs Processes
papers.abstract: A composite Higgs arising from an underlying strong sector generally has non-local interactions with the elementary sector, formulated in terms of momentum-dependent form factors. We construct the minimal Ball-Chiu-type vertices consistent with gauge-invariant non-local $\bar{t}th$ couplings containing Wilson lines, where recursive Ward-Takahashi identities connect the Yukawa interaction to higher-order contact interactions. For a symmetric monopole form factor motivated by lowest-resonance dominance, we compute the top-loop contributions to $gg \to h$ and $h \to \gamma\gamma$ amplitudes in closed form, and demonstrate a logarithmically enhanced deviation from the Standard Model. Current measurements at the LHC exclude the characteristic new physics scale below 3.6 TeV at $2\sigma$, while future colliders could extend the sensitivity to approximately 8 TeV.
papers.reason: Form factors and loop-induced processes are highly relevant to the reader's interest in neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling.

papers.title: Muon Collider: Towards the Energy Frontier
papers.abstract: A muon collider has emerged as a compelling candidate for the next energy-frontier particle accelerator, combining the discovery potential of multi-TeV lepton collisions with a footprint and power consumption far smaller than existing or proposed hadron and electron-positron colliders. Advances over the past two decades in high-power targets, muon production and capture, ionization cooling, rapid acceleration, high-field magnets, collider ring design, and machine-detector integration have transformed the concept from a long-term vision into a credible path toward a future flagship facility. This review summarizes the physics opportunities, the accelerator complex's design and status, the unique experimental environment, recent technical achievements, ongoing international R&D, and remaining steps toward realizing a high-energy muon collider by the middle of the century.
papers.reason: A muon collider is a key future facility for neutrino physics, making this review highly relevant.

papers.title: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization. II. Updated constraints and forecasts for the Simons Observatory and LiteBIRD
papers.abstract: We update the constraints on Lorentz-violating electrodynamics from the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Within the minimal Standard Model Extension, we consider the renormalizable CPT-odd and CPT-even operators of the photon sector, which source cosmic birefringence and circular polarization, respectively. Combining Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and South Pole Telescope (SPT) temperature and $E$-mode data with $B$-mode measurements from BICEP/Keck, SPT-3G D1 and SPTpol, we constrain the CPT-odd coefficients to $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|<7.75\times10^{-45}$ GeV and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}|<3.82\times10^{-45}$ GeV at 95% credible level. These are the strongest bounds to date from any probe, and are driven by the SPT-3G D1 $B$-mode data. For the first time in this type of analysis, we also include the Planck PR4 $EB$ spectrum, which yields a mild preference for a non-zero $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|$. For the CPT-even coefficient, we find $k_{F,E+B}<5.99\times10^{-32}$. Including the latest circular polarization measurements from the Cosmology Large Angular Scale Surveyor (CLASS) tightens this bound by about 7%. This is the first time that CMB circular polarization data contribute to constraining this coefficient. Finally, we forecast the sensitivity of the Simons Observatory (SO) and LiteBIRD. With linear polarization only, the two experiments are complementary, with SO tightening the CPT-even bound by about 30% and LiteBIRD the CPT-odd ones by 40 to 45%. Exploiting the sensitivity to circular polarization provided by the non-idealities of its half-wave plate, LiteBIRD could also improve the CPT-even bound by more than an order of magnitude.
papers.reason: Probing BSM physics via CMB polarization is highly relevant to the reader's interest in precision probes and BSM physics.

papers.title: Feebly-Interacting Particle Searches
papers.abstract: In the last several years, feebly-interacting particles (FIPs) have moved from "exotica" to the mainstream of particle physics. This development is fueled by three motivations: FIPs are one of two broad possibilities for new particles, FIPs are as well motivated by dark matter as WIMPs, and FIPs are connected to important problems in particle physics. I review these motivations and then briefly highlight recent progress in a few areas, including axion-like particles, dark photons and other gauge bosons, the X17 anomaly, quirks, and the Forward Physics Facility.
papers.reason: A high-level review of feebly-interacting particles, which is highly relevant to BSM searches at neutrino experiments.

papers.title: Perturbative QCD Analysis for the Electric Dipole Moment of $\Xi$ and $\Sigma$ Hyperons from CP-Violating Dipole Interactions
papers.abstract: Hyperon electric dipole moments (EDMs) probe CP-violating interactions beyond the Standard Model. Motivated by the recent BESIII measurement [Ablikim et al., Science 393, 1027] and the perturbative QCD analysis of the $\Lambda$ EDM form factor $d_\Lambda$ [Chen et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 051902], we extend the perturbative QCD calculation of the EDM form factor to the $\Xi$ and $\Sigma$ hyperons. We derive factorization formulas from quark EDM and chromoelectric dipole moment contributions in terms of leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs). Using lattice-QCD results for the LCDAs and the strange-quark dipole moment ranges inferred from the BESIII $d_\Lambda$ bound and neutron EDM constraints, we obtain the conditional estimates $-4.8 \times 10^{-18} < d_{\Xi^-} < 1.8\times10^{-18}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $-6.1\times10^{-19} < d_{\Sigma^+} < 2.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ at the scale of ${J/\psi}$ mass. Dedicated searches at BESIII and the future Super Tau-Charm Factory could further constrain these quark-level sources of CP violation.
papers.reason: Perturbative QCD analysis of EDM form factors is highly relevant to the reader's interest in nucleon structure and CP violation.

papers.title: $B\to K a$ decays in QCD factorization and revised bounds on ALP couplings
papers.abstract: Rare flavor-changing processes such as $B\to K a$ offer sensitive probes of axion-like particles (ALPs) for masses below a few GeV. We study this process in the framework of QCD factorization and ALP effective theory, in which the ALP couples to the Standard Model (SM) fermions through shift-invariant derivative interactions. In contrast to previous studies, where flavor violation arises solely from flavor-changing ALP couplings, we also include the contributions proportional to flavor-conserving ALP couplings, in which the flavor change is mediated by the weak interactions of the SM. Based on this analysis, we derive upper bounds on both flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP couplings at low energies. Then we consider the UV scenario of a "minimally flavor-violating ALP", which features flavor-universal ALP-fermion couplings at very high energies, and evaluate the resulting constraints on the UV couplings.

papers.title: Probing $\tau$ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders
papers.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of future multi-TeV muon colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $\tau$ lepton within the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We consider $\tau^+\tau^-$ production through $\mu^+\mu^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $\tau$ production, and the radiative Higgs decay $H\to\tau^+\tau^-\gamma$. At high energies, the dipole-induced contributions quadratic in the Wilson coefficients become particularly important, with associated Higgs production, $\mu^+\mu^-\to\tau^+\tau^-H$, providing the strongest sensitivity through energy-enhanced contact interactions. The remaining channels offer complementary probes of the underlying dipole operators. For a $10$~TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, we obtain combined sensitivities at the nominal $95\%$ confidence level of $|\Delta a_\tau|<1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_\tau|<6.6\times10^{-20}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|\Delta a_\tau^Z|<1.8\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_\tau^Z|<1.0\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$. Compared with FCC-ee projections, the muon collider offers substantially stronger sensitivity to the electric dipole moments, while both facilities offer complementary probes of magnetic dipole moments. These results motivate further studies incorporating realistic detector effects and systematic uncertainties.

papers.title: Triangle singularity with different dynamical couplings
papers.abstract: We carry out a systematic study of the impact of dynamical couplings of the vertices on the manifestations of the triangle singularity (TS) in the loop amplitude. Twelve combinations of external and internal spin-parity quantum numbers, covering the $PPS$, $VPP$, $VVP$, $VPA$, $VVV$, $VVA$, and $VVS$ effective vertices, are enumerated. Each loop amplitude is reduced via the Passarino--Veltman decomposition into scalar integrals $A_{0}$, $B_{0}$, and $C_{0}$, whose Lorentz-scalar coefficients encode the dynamical content of the vertices. Using the masses and kinematics of the $\eta(1405)\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ transition via the $K^{*}\bar{K}K$ loop with the intermediate $f_{0}(980)$ resonance in the $\pi^+\pi^-$ invariant spectrum as a common numerical benchmark for the twelve spin-parity assignments, we find that the same loop topology produces three distinct phenomena which manifest through the lineshapes, i.e. a narrow peak dominated by the $C_{0}$ contribution; a suppressed peak in which the $B_{0}$ and $C_{0}$ function contributions are comparable; and a cusp-like profile in which the coefficient of the leading Landau logarithm vanishes at the physical TS point. These results indicate that the visibility of a TS enhancement is not fixed by the Landau condition alone but reshaped by the detailed dynamics involved in the loop transitions.
papers.reason: Dynamical couplings in loop amplitudes are highly relevant to the reader's interest in neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling.

papers.title: Nuclear mass calculation based on anisotropic kernel ridge regression and $\alpha$-decay chain recursion
papers.abstract: Many short-lived or rarely produced nuclei defy direct mass spectrometry, but their masses are constrained by the $\alpha$-decay energies connecting them through decay chains. We combine anisotropic kernel ridge regression (AKRR), an extended Garvey--Kelson relation (GK16), and $\alpha$-decay chain recursion: AKRR learns the residuals between experimental $\alpha$-decay energies and WS4 predictions, GK16 removes residual local fluctuations, and the corrected energies convert a measured anchor mass into the target mass by exact recursion---replacing absolute-mass extrapolation with interpolation of relative decay energies plus exact algebra. The only data-adjusted quantities are the three kernel hyperparameters, fixed by leave-one-out cross validation. For the 22 nuclei whose masses were measured only after AME2003, the $Q_\alpha$ RMSD falls from 169~keV (WS4) to 108~keV (AKRR) and 65~keV (AKRR+GK16), and the mass-excess RMSD reaches 86~keV, versus 348 and 211~keV for WS4 and AKRR. Mass excesses are further predicted for the 122 nuclei with measured $Q_\alpha$ but no directly measured masses.
papers.reason: Nuclear structure and mass calculations are relevant to the reader's interest in nuclear physics for neutrino experiments.

papers.title: Strangeness-to-entropy ratio across the QCD crossover
papers.abstract: We study the absolute open-strangeness density $n_{|S|}$ of strongly interacting matter at vanishing conserved-charge chemical potentials. Unlike the net-strangeness susceptibility $\chi_2^S$, this quantity is not a derivative of the QCD partition function and requires a microscopic specification of the strangeness carriers. We use an equation of state that interpolates between an interacting hadron resonance gas and a quark-gluon plasma, with parameters fixed previously by lattice-QCD bulk thermodynamics. The ratio of $n_{|S|}$ to the entropy density $s$ follows the hadron-gas behavior below $T\simeq120$ MeV, rises above the ideal massless $2+1$-flavor limit of approximately $0.053$ across the crossover, and approaches this limit from above at high temperature. The same equation of state, minimally extended to finite $\mu_S$, captures the temperature dependence of the lattice-QCD $\chi_2^S$. For uncorrelated singly-strange Boltzmann particles, the strangeness fluctuation factor $F_S=\chi_2^S/(n_{|S|}/T^3)$ equals unity. Within the constructed equation of state, it deviates from unity by less than $10\%$. This allows us to estimate $n_{|S|}/s$ from lattice-QCD data on $\chi_2^S$ and $s$. The lattice-based estimate reaches a maximum of $n_{|S|}/s\simeq0.063$ at $T\simeq220$ MeV, followed by a $20\%$ decrease towards the high-temperature limit.
papers.reason: Relevant to the reader's interest in QCD thermodynamics and strangeness carriers in nuclear matter.

papers.title: Loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ at NLO+PS for LHC simulations: exact, fast scale and PDF event weights, theory uncertainties, and the limits of rescaled LO+PS
papers.abstract: We study loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ production with charged-lepton and neutrino $Z$ decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD matched to parton showers, using public software at $\sqrt{s}=13$ and 13.6 TeV. An exact loop-amplitude cache reduces event-generation time by a factor of 26 with 450 scale and PDF weights, while Born suppression improves boosted-event statistics without changing the weighted prediction. We present inclusive results for both channels and charged-lepton differential and STXS Stage 1.3 predictions with theory uncertainties. At 13.6 TeV, fixed-order top-quark mass-scheme variations transferred to NLO+PS dominate the statistically precise central-Higgs STXS bins for $p_\mathrm{T}^V\ge150$ GeV, reaching 32-50%. An inclusive $K$ factor does not reproduce the boosted and jet-dependent NLO+PS spectra of the tested LO+PS samples, and the differences depend strongly on the shower prescription. For specified CMS- and ATLAS-style vetoed sources at 13.6 TeV, we construct separate charged-lepton and neutrino corrections using ensembles of gradient-boosted classifiers, with calibration, target-theory variations and transfer uncertainties. Independent tests show substantial improvement over inclusive rescaling in most tested distributions, but not uniform closure. In charged-lepton calibration comparisons, the median STXS uncertainty from transported NLO scales and transfer terms is 17% for both the CMS- and ATLAS-style corrections, compared with LO scale uncertainties of 28% and 26% at fixed $K$. These comparisons do not include the complete target-theory budget. The corrections do not restore the depleted hard-recoil population; the highest ATLAS-style $p_\mathrm{T}^H$ bin stays below NLO+PS even at the upper edge of its band. The setup, reference results, and source- and channel-specific models support new NLO+PS generation and reuse of existing samples within stated limits.
papers.reason: Precision QCD calculations and NLO+PS are relevant to the reader's interest in event generators and interaction modeling.

papers.title: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
papers.abstract: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, mostly on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, which also implement global symmetries and their anomalies consistently, but allow the high-energy behavior to better match real QCD.
papers.reason: Holographic approaches to hadron structure are relevant for understanding nucleon form factors and QCD inputs for neutrino scattering.

papers.title: Mapping the multimessenger horizon for $\gamma$-ray counterparts of cosmic neutrinos
papers.abstract: The joint detection of high-energy neutrinos and $\gamma$-rays offers a powerful probe of the most energetic astrophysical accelerators, linking hadronic interactions to observable signatures across cosmic distances. Understanding the conditions under which these two messengers can be simultaneously observed is essential for identifying and characterizing the sources of cosmic neutrinos. In this work, we examine the detectability of $\gamma$-ray cascades associated with neutrino production in source environments that are gamma-ray transparent, focusing on how electromagnetic cascades evolve as $\gamma$-rays propagate through intergalactic space. By modeling photon interactions with the extragalactic background light and deflections in intergalactic magnetic fields, we determine the minimum neutrino fluence for transient emission and neutrino flux for steady emission required to produce a $\gamma$-ray counterpart detectable by $\gamma$-ray observatories, such as Fermi-LAT, HAWC, or LHAASO. This defines a ``multimessenger horizon" -- the region in flux-distance parameter space where neutrinos and $\gamma$-rays are jointly observable. We consider both energy-binned injection tied to IceCube's sensitivity and a continuous power-law spectrum extending from TeV to PeV energies. Our results reveal that detectability depends strongly on redshift, magnetic field strength, and photon energy, with higher-energy cascades suffering greater attenuation inside filamentary structures. The framework provides new constraints on source opacity, baryon loading, and neutrino production mechanisms, offering a predictive tool for interpreting current events and guiding future multimessenger campaigns.
papers.reason: This paper addresses the detection of high-energy neutrinos and their gamma-ray counterparts, which is relevant to the reader's interest in neutrino phenomenology.

papers.title: Effects of QCD Equation of State on Cosmological Parameters and Stochastic Gravitational-Waves Spectrum
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic evolution of the early Universe across the QCD crossover and up to the electroweak (EW) scale, emphasizing the systematic impact of the QCD equation of state (EoS) and electroweak degrees of freedom on thermodynamic variables, cosmological parameters, and gravitational-wave observables. Using the HotQCD EoS as a baseline, we employ Gaussian Process (GP) regression to generate ensembles of 1000 thermodynamically consistent EoS samples, each extrapolated to high temperatures with and without EW contributions. For each ensemble, we solve the Friedmann equations to obtain the expansion history and compute gravitational-wave (GW) observables, including the instantaneous spectral tilt $n_{gw}(f)$ and the normalized GW energy density $\Omega_{gw}(f)/\Omega_{gw}^{\rm rad}$. We find that including the EW sector is the dominant effect across all observables, outweighing differences among QCD baseline models that share the same lattice calibration. In particular, EW contributions drive the EoS toward the radiation-dominated limit earlier, reduce excursions of the speed of sound toward the causality bound, suppress transient fluctuations in the Hubble and kinematic parameters near $t \sim 10^{-5}$ s, and qualitatively change the GW spectrum from a strongly frequency-dependent signal to a flat, suppressed plateau. These results demonstrate that accurate modeling of the electroweak sector is essential for an unbiased extraction of QCD-era physics from the stochastic gravitational-wave background.
papers.reason: The QCD equation of state and its impact on the early universe is highly relevant to the reader's interest in neutrino-nucleus interactions and nuclear physics.

papers.title: Active Galactic Nuclei as Beyond the Standard Model Laboratories: a White Paper
papers.abstract: Multi-messenger and multi-wavelength observations of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) can provide otherwise inaccessible knowledge about physics Beyond the Standard Model (BSM), and may even lead to its discovery. Realizing this potential hinges on two parallel efforts: advancing our understanding of AGN and of the dark matter around them, and identifying the BSM signatures that are at once promising and robust against the gaps in that understanding. These fields have attracted growing interest in recent years, also motivated by the IceCube association of neutrinos to individual AGN, yet we have only begun to explore their cross-fertilization. This white paper offers a new perspective on this interdisciplinary endeavor. It concisely reviews the state of the art in each field and at their interface, and identifies the key open questions that must be addressed to strengthen our prospects for learning about BSM physics with AGN.
papers.reason: Interdisciplinary white paper on AGN as BSM labs, relevant for neutrino astronomy and dark matter connections.

papers.title: Top-Quark Physics after Evidence for Toponium
papers.abstract: The top quark decays before it hadronizes, and toponium, the t\bar t bound state, was long thought unobservable as a resonance. CMS and ATLAS each report an excess of top-quark pairs at threshold, above five standard deviations over fixed-order quantum chromodynamics (QCD), and CMS confirms it in a second decay channel. Its angular distributions match the color-singlet pseudoscalar quasi-bound state \eta_t of nonrelativistic QCD, although an additional pseudoscalar boson is not excluded and higher-order fixed-order QCD accounts for part of the enhancement. We review the theory, ATLAS's nominal Green's-function signal model, and the measurements, whose cross sections range from about 3 to 13 pb. Part of the spread comes from the signal model and part persists between analyses using the same model. We discuss consequences for entanglement, the top mass, and heavy-pseudoscalar searches. We then review the top-quark program, from mass definitions to electroweak precision, flavor, the charge-conjugation and parity (CP) structure of the top Yukawa coupling, supersymmetry, multi-top production, and effective field theory. We close with prospects at the High-Luminosity LHC and future colliders, where an e^+e^- threshold scan can determine the top-quark mass in a short-distance scheme to a few tens of MeV.
papers.reason: Relevant to top-quark physics and entanglement, though somewhat peripheral to the reader's neutrino focus.

papers.title: Impact of errors-on-errors on the PDF determination from combined HERA data
papers.abstract: We study how the determination of parton distribution functions (PDFs) from the combined HERA inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering data is affected when the quoted sizes of the systematic errors are themselves treated as uncertain. We refer to these uncertainties informally as errors-on-errors and account for them using the Gamma Variance Model, which treats the squared quoted systematic errors as Gamma-distributed estimates of unknown variances. As a result, the usual quadratic nuisance parameter constraints in the $\chi^2$ are replaced with logarithmic ones. We present two applications of the framework. In the first, a robustness test estimates the largest errors-on-errors effects that could be present in our reproduction of the HERAPDF2.0 NNLO fit, reducing $\chi^2/n_{\rm dof}$ from 1363/1131 to 1306/1131, with the main impact concentrated at low Bjorken $x$ and low squared momentum transfer, $Q^2$. Comparable reductions are observed with a more flexible small-$x$ parametrisation, both at fixed NNLO and with NNLO+NLL$_x$ resummation. In the second, the error-on-error parameters are instead assigned a priori, as they would be in a PDF determination intended for publication. Taken together, the results indicate that errors-on-errors can account for a substantial part of the apparent data-theory tension in the combined HERA dataset, improving the inferred compatibility and widening the fitted PDF uncertainties without appreciably displacing the PDFs or cross-section predictions themselves.
papers.reason: Relevant to the reader's interest in systematic uncertainties and precision QCD.

papers.title: Signatures of Leptophilic Baryogenesis at Muon Colliders
papers.abstract: The baryon asymmetry of the Universe may be produced in a model with 3 Higgs fields, a Higgs Troika, without the need for a strong first order electroweak phase transition. The couplings of the new Higgs fields to Standard Model fermions are assumed in accord with the "Spontaneous Flavor Violation (SFV)" framework, in order to avoid large deviations from flavor physics constraints. We consider a leptophilic version of SFV and outline its potential signatures at future muon colliders, envisioned to be multi-TeV partonic center of momentum machines. Hence, they provide optimal venues to search for the leptophilic Higgs Troika baryogenesis mechanism. The projected reach for signals of the new scalars allows for probing the key components of the baryogenesis model at scales that accommodate cosmological requirements.
papers.reason: Muon collider physics is a medium-interest topic for this reader, specifically regarding neutrino beams and BSM searches.

papers.title: Absolute luminosity calibration of the LHCb detector in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with beam-gas imaging
papers.abstract: An absolute calibration of the luminosity for proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with the LHCb detector in Run 2 of the LHC is presented. The calibration cross-section of the Vertex counter, a statistic based on reconstructed primary vertices, is measured using the beam-gas imaging method to be $\sigma_\mathrm{Vertex} = 57.61 \pm 0.06\ (stat) \pm 0.52\ (syst)$ mb, corresponding to a relative precision of 0.91%. This result provides around a factor of two improvement in the precision of the LHCb luminosity calibration used in previous cross-section measurements with this dataset. The largest systematic uncertainties arise from the imperfect knowledge of the beam-gas vertex resolution, the observed fill-by-fill spread of the cross-section, and the choice of transverse beam-profile fit model.
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca

papers.title: Thermal Composite Dark Matter at LZ
papers.abstract: We show that stable fermionic resonances of Composite Higgs models provide a thermal inelastic Dark Matter interpretation of the high-energy nuclear-recoil event LZ230616. Their stability follows from an exact accidental parity of the strong sector. Annihilation channels from composite interactions link the thermal relic mass to the strong coupling, allowing masses well beyond the pure electroweak prediction. We identify three scenarios in which the neutral states form a split pseudo-Dirac pair, distinguished by the origin of the inelastic coupling to the $Z$ boson. In the pure electroweak regime, the pair consists of the neutral components of a complex Higgsino-like doublet. Its unsuppressed inelastic $Z$ coupling requires Dark Matter masses above 20 TeV. In the pure strong regime, the suppressed $Z$ coupling of neutral states with vanishing hypercharge arises from strong interactions alone, allowing for smaller splittings and TeV-scale masses. In the third regime, which interpolates between the previous two, the neutral components of multiplets with different hypercharge are mixed. This enhances their inelastic coupling, accommodating the LZ event for masses of a few TeV and splittings around 300 keV, with mixing angles of order $10^\circ$. All three cases provide a thermal Dark Matter candidate able to explain the LZ event, consistently with the solar-capture bounds, the LZ high-energy sideband, and gamma-ray indirect searches.

papers.title: Analytic next-to-leading order electroweak corrections to Higgs boson pair production in the forward limit
papers.abstract: We calculate next-to-leading order electroweak corrections for Higgs boson pair production in the gluon fusion channel, in the forward limit. We perform an analytic calculation and obtain a final result for the partonic cross section that depends explicitly on all kinematic parameters and particle masses. We describe our method, which can be readily applied to similar processes. We observe rapid convergence within the validity range of the forward expansion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the entire phase space can be covered when this approach is combined with the high-energy expansion.
papers.reason: NLO electroweak corrections are relevant to precision physics, though not directly to neutrino-nucleus scattering.

papers.title: A new angle on coherence-violating logarithms in color-singlet processes
papers.abstract: We introduce a new formulation for the resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the transverse energy flow in rapidity gaps in the Drell-Yan process. Our formalism allows us to resum coherence-violating logarithms in the gap cross section in the phenomenologically important regime where the gap size is comparable to the logarithm of the transverse energy. In the formal small gap limit, our result reduces to the known state-of-the-art resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the Drell-Yan process. However, we identify sizable new corrections even for moderate gap widths that significantly modify the phenomenological picture for LHC applications. This work will form an important element of future extensions to a range of global and non-global observables.
papers.reason: QCD resummation techniques are relevant to the reader's interest in hadronization and scattering systematics.

papers.title: Double parton scattering singularities in two-loop gluon-fusion amplitudes
papers.abstract: Gluon fusion to two massive colour singlets can develop a double parton scattering (DPS) singularity as $p_T\to0$: each gluon splits, and its daughters fuse pairwise. We determine two-loop logarithms using a common kernel and derive finite matching functions analytically for gluon and quark splittings. Normalised to one loop, the cubic coefficient changes sign between channels. Complete $gg\to HH$, $gg\to AA$ and $gg\to ZZ$ amplitudes confirm the predicted colour, helicity and parity dependence and phase. The kernel gives leading DPS logarithms for other pairs with this DPS configuration.
papers.reason: Relevant to QCD resummation and scattering, though not directly to neutrino-nucleus interactions.

papers.title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincar\'e algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.
papers.reason: Relevant to the reader's interest in spin correlations, though focused on hydrodynamics.

papers.title: Universal Mass Equation for Equal-Quantum Excited-States Sets~III
papers.abstract: Using our simple logarithmic Universal Mass Equation, we considered heavy non-$q\bar{q}$ meson states. PDG2026 reported a series of mesons with quantum numbers not allowed for standard $q\bar{q}$ states. Using LQCD predictions, we evaluated a scalar $0^{++}$ and tensor $2^{++}$ glueball series for which predictions are available. This approach allows us to predict heavy states that require future experimental studies. Additionally, we consider the possible misidentification of some meson states.
papers.reason: Relevant to hadron spectroscopy, which is medium-interest.

papers.title: Complete Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-handed Neutrino Loops
papers.abstract: We study the complete cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement. These CC signals are induced by the inflaton-right-handed-neutrino interaction and can be extracted in the collinear squeezed configuration, which allows the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop to be factorized into the hard and soft parts. We precisely compute the soft part of the fermion loop for the first time by using the complete mode functions and the full loop integral, and treat the hard part as a tree-level subdiagram. We subtract the large-momentum asymptotic terms of the soft loop integrand and retain their finite contributions to the oscillation. We then evaluate the full spinor-helicity and Schwinger-Keldysh sums to obtain a finite, closed analytic formula for the complex clock coefficient. We further derive a compact formula for the leading CC signals in the large-chemical-potential expansion. We analyze the structure of the soft-part contribution by examining the sum of residues of the Mellin poles of the fermion propagators. For this, we demonstrate that the first local pole on each soft line contributes half of the asymptotic coefficient on one Schwinger-Keldysh path and the remaining local poles on the second soft line supply the other half.
papers.reason: While it involves right-handed neutrinos, the focus is on cosmological collider signatures rather than the reader's core interest in neutrino-nucleus interactions or low-energy precision physics.

papers.title: A Proposal for Quantum Reference Frames in Quantum Field Theory and their Experimental Exploration
papers.abstract: We construct quantum reference frames (QRFs) in quantum field theory, using localized modes of a scalar field as frames for its shift symmetry. We import tools from relativistic quantum information to explicitly compute entropies and correlation measures of relational observables, investigating their frame dependence and the new features arising from the field-theoretic character of the system. Unlike QRFs for systems with finitely many degrees of freedom, localized field-theoretic QRFs are necessarily mixed in physically relevant states and generically correlated with the subsystems they describe. These aspects of QRFs for fields affect the properties of relational observables in a subtle way. Furthermore, we put forward a proposal for testing these predictions with existing quantum simulators based on ultracold atoms and quantum fluids, thus connecting QRF physics with analogue gravity platforms.
papers.reason: Quantum reference frames in QFT are an interesting theoretical topic, though the focus here is on analogue gravity platforms.

papers.title: Quantum Reference Frames, Locality, and Microcausality in Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract: As a consequence of the relativistic spectrum condition, quantum reference frames for translations on Minkowski space are never described by projection-valued measures, and in many cases fail a weaker spacetime localisation property known as the norm-$1$ condition. This has several implications for the local and observable structure of quantum field theories described relative to even the best available frame: for a large class of frame states, strict locality is replaced by almost locality, and microcausality by commutators that decay rapidly with increasing separation, corresponding to an effective smearing of the light cone by the localisation density of the frame state. Operations built from finitely many almost local Kraus operators, for example nonselective measurements of relativised local observables, satisfy an approximate no-signalling bound, with a residue attributable to the localisation uncertainty of the frame. Whether causality in its strongest operational form -- non-disturbance under all physically realisable operations -- survives relativisation is left open. An upshot of our finding is that quantum field theories formulated relative to a quantum reference frame cannot rest on the traditional axioms, and some general relational axiomatisation must replace at least some of them by taking into account physically realistic properties of the frame.
papers.reason: This paper discusses the implications of quantum reference frames for locality and microcausality in QFT, which is of theoretical interest.

papers.title: Anomaly inflow for simplicial K\"{a}hler fermions
papers.abstract: We study massive K\"{a}hler Dirac fermions propagating on finite triangulations of various three dimensional manifolds with one or more boundaries. To probe the anomaly structure of these models we decompose the K\"{a}hler field into two reduced K\"{a}hler fields and choose boundary conditions that ensure that any edge modes are necessarily massless. We then show how to factorize the Pfaffian of this system into a product of bulk and boundary sectors each of which can separately pick up a phase under a global $Z_4$ transformation of the fermions that simultaneously changes the sign of the mass. These phases are topological, depending only on the index of the lattice K\"{a}hler operator in that sector. For the boundary sector a non-trivial phase signals the presence of a 't Hooft anomaly. We study cases where the boundary is anomalous but an inflow from the bulk cancels its phase. Canceling this anomaly for a non-orientable boundary in the absence of the bulk recovers the known classification of topological superconductors. We also give a continuum interpretation of these results in terms of inflow from a gravitational Chern Simons theory which is induced by integrating out massive bulk K\"{a}hler Dirac fermions. In the presence of a boundary the latter gives rise to Wen-Zee terms that mediate the anomaly inflow mechanism.
papers.reason: Anomaly inflow and topological phases are relevant to the reader's interest in EFTs for precision physics.

papers.title: Axion electrodynamics and the advection-diffusion structure of TEM modes in hollow-conductor waveguides
papers.abstract: We present a systematic investigation of transverse electromagnetic (TEM) modes in hollow-conductor waveguides filled with a dielectric medium described by axion electrodynamics. While such modes do not propagate in conventional single-conductor waveguides, the coupling of the axion field to an external magnetic field enables their propagation. We show that the resulting TEM modes are governed by an advection-diffusion-type equation for the transverse electrostatic potential, establishing a direct mathematical connection between axion electrodynamics and advection-diffusion phenomena. We illustrate this connection through explicit solutions and field profiles for cylindrical waveguides, considering uniform and rigid rotational drift fields, both individually and in combination, as well as different values of the parameter controlling the advection-to-diffusion ratio (P\'eclet number). These results establish a transport-based framework for understanding how spatial variations of the axion-electrodynamics background shape the transverse electromagnetic fields in hollow-conductor waveguides.

papers.title: 21 cm Cosmology of Boosted Dark Matter
papers.abstract: The formation history of low-mass halos is sensitive to the properties of dark matter. At low redshift, nonlinear evolution and baryonic processes can obscure this information. The 21 cm signal provides access to a high-redshift stage of structure formation, when the abundance and clustering of low-mass halos retain direct sensitivity to the mass and interactions of dark matter. Boosted dark matter (BDM) realizes this possibility through a two-component scenario in which the annihilation of the heavier component converts part of the mass difference into kinetic energy of the lighter component. Self-interactions redistribute this energy and generate pressure support, suppressing small-scale density perturbations even for dark matter masses in the MeV range. papers.title: 'Forward-backward' flows and integration cycles for semiclassical Euclidean gravity

We obtain the same elliptic curve families by specializing the complexified mass parameters of the rank-1 $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$ theories, with holonomies motivated by the 7-brane insertions required by the S-fold prescription. The two constructions agree in Weierstrass form. The families with continuous mass deformations organize into characters of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{g}_2$, consistently with their singular fibers. Finally, we discuss that the Seiberg--Witten curves for $\mathbb{Z}_n$ S-folds can be obtained through cyclic $n$-isogenies, which may provide a uniform quotient curve description of rank-1 S-folds.
